data.name: Gopaal
data.gender_notes: Gopaal is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Gopaal is a name derived from the Sanskrit language, meaning 'Protector of Cows and People'. In Hindu mythology, Lord Gopaal is an avatar of Lord Vishnu who is often depicted as a cowherd. He is believed to be the protector and preserver of all beings, and is revered for his compassionate and nurturing nature. The name Gopaal carries the meaning “Protector of Cows and People” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Gopaal usually hope their child will grow to embody protector of cows and people and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Gopaal belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Protector of Cows and People.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Gopaal total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.spiritual_significance: Gopaal's name encapsulates the concept of divine protection and love. In Hindu philosophy, he represents spiritual nourishment and self-sacrifice, as He is the Protector of all creatures – both bovine and human. Hindu devotional texts often describe Lord Gopaal as a caregiver and healer, invoking feelings of humility, devotion, and surrender. He is a reminder of the divine grace and compassion that dwells within us and is embodied in the form of a nurturing, protective deity.
